title: An exception firewall
description:
Stop C++ exceptions at a C boundary and turn them into error codes.

```
lib_parse("42")   -> OK, 42
lib_parse("x")    -> ERR_INVALID ("not a number: x")
lib_parse(nullptr) -> ERR_NULL
lib_last_error()  -> "not a number: x"
```
hints: Wrap the whole body in one `try` and put every `catch` after it; each `catch` sets the message and returns its code (lesson 2.06).
Mark it `noexcept` too: then a missed exception ends the program at once instead of crossing into C code.
requirements: `extern "C" int lib_parse(const char* text, int* out)` returns an error code and never lets an exception escape.
Keep the last error message in one library-wide `std::string` (a global in the library), readable through `extern "C" const char* lib_last_error()`, which returns its `c_str()`.
stretch: Write a template `guard(f)` that wraps any function body the same way, like lesson 2.06's barrier. Then make the message per thread: look up the `thread_local` keyword (lesson 2.04 mentions it), which gives every thread its own copy of a variable so two threads cannot overwrite each other's last error.
